extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, and lawyers facing or handling USPTO reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, and the sanctions/obligations that may be ordered when a practitioner is suspended by a State authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a State authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order requested that the Director impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of California in In re Jerry Lane Hefner, S229431.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the State's discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file a response opposing reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a response may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for opposing reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may oppose imposition of reciprocal discipline by asserting one or more reasons set out in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the specific § 11.24(d)(1) reasons are not restated in full on the page, the Notice allowed Respondent to oppose on those statutory/regulatory grounds; absence of such a response was treated as creating no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation predicated on 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (suspension on consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline here was predicated on violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), i.e., being suspended on consent from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the action is based on Respondent's violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon the state suspension on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension term and partial suspension structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may order suspension from practice before the USPTO for a specified term, possibly with all but a portion stayed (i.e., suspended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, Respondent is suspended for one (1) year, with all but 90 days suspended; the Order states suspension effective the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation requirement accompanying suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may place the respondent on a period of probation following or concurrent with suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, Respondent is placed on probation for two (2) years effective the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to take and pass the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may be ordered to take and pass the MPRE within a specified time as a condition of discipline or reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here the Respondent shall take and pass the MPRE within one year of the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, its basis, and any conditions imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs publication of a Notice of Suspension containing respondent identity, registration number, a short description of the discipline, the regulatory provision violated, and the factual predicate (e.g., state suspension reasons). An example Notice text is included in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is admitted, and to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with the duties set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as part of the discipline/order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically requires Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (the text of § 11.58 is not reproduced on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and revocation of PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs that the USPTO dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the PKI certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or being added to Customer Numbers until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplined respondent may be prohibited from applying for, obtaining, or being added to any USPTO Customer Number until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain one, nor have his name added to a Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are made available for public review at the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites that disciplinary decisions are available at: http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis/factual predicates for state discipline may inform USPTO action
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual bases for the underlying state suspension (e.g., criminal convictions, rule violations, failure to comply with state rules) are noted and form the predicate for reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order recounts the state suspension was based upon (1) felony conviction for possession of a controlled substance; (2) misdemeanor conviction for carrying a loaded firearm in public; and (3) violation of rule 9.20 of the California Rules of Court and §6103 of the California Business and Professional Code due to failure to comply with rule 9.20.
